pages.text: "Oh, a boat is passing!" Lolo left a spoonful of soup and ran to the window. The right chair at the table was empty. On the left, Riri sat munching.
"Lolo, we must finish eating before the pier," Riri said, holding her spoon. "I want to go too! I can eat quickly!" But Lolo set down the spoon and jumped over the threshold.
Much later, Lolo returned and took a spoonful. The soup had cooled to lukewarm. "It does not taste good anymore..." Lolo's shoulders drooped.
Mom hugged Lolo and settled them in the right chair. "Lolo, this chair has a secret." Lolo leaned their nose toward the bowl.
Mom served fresh, steaming soup. "Soup tastes best while it steams. While you are out, all the steam escapes." Lolo touched the bowl. Warm!
Riri planted her bottom in her chair. "Stay in your chair—yum!" Lolo planted their bottom in the chair too. "Stay!" They smiled at each other.
Even when a seagull flew past the window, Lolo resisted getting up. One spoonful, two, three. The soup was still warm. Stay in your chair—yum!
Lolo held up the empty bowl. "Warm right to the last spoonful!" Mom smiled as she took it.
Every evening, Lolo sat in the right chair first. "One, bottom in my chair! Two, spoonfuls while it steams! Three, show the empty bowl!" Lolo set both hands on the table. Steam rose from the bowl.

On the way to the pier, Lolo splashed boots into a puddle. Mom put a hand on Lolo's tummy and hugged them. "Sitting to eat made your tummy warm, right?" Hugging Mom's neck, Lolo said, "Stay in your chair—yum!"
